title: Two variables named incorrectly in WA and GA
description:
Well, I was using our package for an estimator's case study and found... an issue. 

In data-raw/wa/01-forested.R, lines 38 & 39 we have: 

```
    temp_annual_min = tmin,
    temp_january_min = tmin_annual,
```

inside of a `rename()`. But really, it should be: 

```
    temp_annual_min = tmin_annual,
    temp_january_min = tmin,
```

The same typo occurs in data-raw/ga/01-forested-ga.R, lines 38 & 39. 

I am not sure what is "best practice" here since it is a data package, and we'd like that data to be consistent across versions. Maybe we should just update the documentation? Or should we update the data and document it? Or something else? 

I should note I only came across this because I was working with the FIA rasters themselves, and needed my extracted values from those rasters to match up with the data in `forested`. That is to say (almost) all users would never come across this.

title: scale of temperature variables
description: The temperatures are documented as degrees Celcius * 100. Why not just degrees Celcius?

title: reproduce `forested` from source rasters
description:
I've got a set of source rasters locally that Grayson "clipped" from the national level data to just WA; we can use them to build `wa_plts.rds` from `00-wa_plts.R`. I reran `00-wa_plts.R` and see:

1) A few hundred very, very small changes in lat/lon.
2) Two rows ended up with bad (all-zero) data and `NA` `land_type`.

...and no changes otherwise.

We can't track the rasters as GH has a hard 100MB limit. Altogether, the uncompressed rasters are around 900MB (or ~130MB compressed.)

Going to omit those two corrupted rows and keep on truckin. 🚛
